balance.reason: Milk is a daily habit category where switching is won slowly at the doorstep and chiller, but the '4am/named-farmer' recognition asset is the only durable competitive moat against Amul and Nandini — hold brand at 60 for the year so each activation burst starts from a rising baseline, not a flat one; the 57/43 the channels actually add up to is close enough that a small budget tilt toward the TV lead channel closes it.

rows.statement: Grow Heritage Pure Milk volume by 1.2X  converting daily loose/unbranded milk buyers to branded packs in the South India core, then extend the same conversion motion nationally.
Move 20% of the 25–44 household milk buyer from loose or a rival pack to a repeat Heritage daily purchase, and hold that repeat via general trade and home delivery.
rows.measure: repeat purchase rate among converted households; packs sold per household per week

rows.statement: Make 'milked at dawn, on your table by morning — quality-checked every single day' the reason a daily buyer trusts a Heritage pack over loose milk at the point of purchase.
rows.measure: prompted association of Heritage with 'same-day / quality-checked purity' vs Amul/Nandini/loose; message recall among 25–44 mothers

rows.audience: The 25–44 household milk buyer (mother) currently buying a rival pack daily, in the South India core
rows.believes_now: Loose milk from the local vendor is fresh and cheaper; branded packs are 'processed' and I'm paying for a name. I don't distrust Heritage — I've just never had a reason to switch the daily habit.

rows.audience: The daily buyer at the point of purchase — deciding between packs at the GT chiller, the person the POSM strip and promoter actually meet
rows.believes_now: At the chiller they're all similar; I'll pick on price or whichever is stocked front. 'Same-day' and 'quality-checked' would move me if I believed it at the moment I reach for a pack.

rows.audience: GT retailers and distributors in the South India core who decide chiller facing and repeat stocking
rows.believes_now: Loose milk still moves; Amul and Nandini are the safe branded bets. Heritage moves daily but I'll give front-of-chiller to whoever sells through and doesn't sit.
rows.pillar: functional — 'Heritage moves every day and now carries a same-day, quality-checked story your shoppers trust over loose.' Sell-through and repeat, not consumer emotion, is what moves this audience.

rows.job: Carry the sourced 4am/named-farmer story to the South India core to build recognition — reach, not proof of the functional claim, which has no sourced RTB
rows.measure: Coverage and cost per reach against 25–44 milk buyers in core states

rows.job: 'Milked at dawn. On your table by morning.' — the farmer's face near residential clusters, building recognition for the daily buyer
rows.measure: Coverage and cost per reach in target residential catchments

rows.job: Reach the 25–44 mother researching what she buys with the timestamp-to-tumbler cut; do NOT judge on the functional claim landing — it can't be proven here
rows.measure: 6s view-through and cost per reach against the mother segment

rows.job: Get existing buyers to carry the two-milk-moments story — first tumbler, last glass — with the dawn footage spliced in
Promoter shows the dated pack and farmer card and offers a taste — physical demonstration at the doorstep turns the rank-1 mother's habit; this is field proof, not media proof
rows.measure: Trial-to-switch rate and cost per acquired daily household

rows.job: 'Quality-checked every single day' at the chiller for the rank-2 buyer choosing between packs — asserts the claim at the moment of reach; carries the assertion, does not verify it
rows.measure: Sell-through rate at stocked stores vs control; front-chiller pack pickup

rows.job: Move the rank-3 retailer on sell-through and repeat: 'Heritage moves every day, front the chiller' — a stocking/facing decision, not consumer emotion
rows.measure: Front-of-chiller facings won, repeat order rate, distribution depth

rows.occasion: The first tumbler before school — the morning milk decision the 25–44 mother makes for her child
rows.channels: TV (40s, 4am film) [lead] · OOH (highway + neighbourhood hoarding) · Digital pre-roll (20s)
rows.hands_over: Recognition of the named farmer and the 'milked at dawn, on your table by morning' story in the South India core — so that when the promoter knocks and the chiller strip appears, the buyer already knows the face. Reach channels only; no proof of the functional claim, which has no sourced RTB.

rows.phase: 2 · Turn recognition into the daily habit
rows.occasion: The switch from loose/unbranded milk to a standing daily Heritage pack — the household's repeat purchase decision
rows.channels: On-ground (RWA/society morning stall) [lead] · POSM (chiller strip + door cling) · Trade (distributor + GT retailer pitch)
rows.hands_over: Trialled households who switched, and front-of-chiller facings won at GT — a base of daily buyers and the shelf position needed to keep serving them. Field demonstration does the proving here; media only carries the assertion.

rows.phase: 3 · Hold the habit and let buyers carry it
rows.occasion: The last glass before bed — the everyday nutrition moment repeated by households already buying, now spread by them
rows.channels: Social (Reel/Short, mother POV) [lead] · sustaining OOH · sustaining chiller POSM
rows.hands_over: Advocacy and sentiment from existing daily buyers feeding back into reach — the two-milk-moments story carried by mothers, not media. Rolls into the next annual cycle's phase 1 with an established buyer base to defend.

rows.occasion: The first tumbler before school and the last glass before bed — the two everyday milk moments, before any switch is asked for
rows.channels: TV (40s, 4am film) [lead]; OOH (highway + neighbourhood hoarding); Digital pre-roll (20s)
rows.hands_over: A South India core that recognises the 4am/named-farmer story and the daily-milk claim, so the doorstep promoter isn't a cold knock — the face on the hoarding is already familiar when the stall arrives

rows.occasion: The morning milk decision at the society gate — the daily buyer choosing today's pack over loose/unbranded
rows.channels: On-ground (RWA/society morning stall) [lead]; POSM (chiller strip + door cling); Social (Reel/Short) sustaining recognition alongside
rows.hands_over: Households that have tasted, seen the dated pack and the farmer card, and made one switch — plus the retail chiller primed with POSM so the second purchase has somewhere to land

rows.occasion: The repeat morning — turning one switch into the standing daily buy, tumbler after tumbler
rows.channels: Trade (distributor + GT retailer pitch) [lead]; POSM (chiller strip + door cling); Social (Reel/Short, mother POV) for advocacy
rows.hands_over: Front-of-chiller facings held, repeat order rate established, and existing buyers carrying the two-moments story outward — feeding recognition back into the next recognition wave

rows.leading: Cost per reach and cumulative 1+ coverage against 25–44 milk buyers in the South India core, tracked weekly across TV, OOH and digital pre-roll; 6s view-through on the pre-roll cut
rows.lagging: Aided and unaided brand recognition of the 'milked at dawn / same-day' story in core states, measured pre- vs post-burst; movement in spontaneous brand awareness vs Amul, Nandini, Dodla, Arokya
rows.would_tell_us_it_failed: By the end of the first burst: cost per reach runs materially above the media plan's benchmark, OR post-wave recognition of the dawn/farmer story has not moved above the pre-wave baseline. If the story is being seen but not remembered, the reach spend is buying impressions, not memory — pause and re-cut before the next flight.

rows.leading: Participation on the Reel/Short — shares, saves, and volume of UGC replicating the two-milk-moments format — plus sentiment split, tracked weekly
rows.lagging: Sustained share of positive brand conversation and organic mentions of #PureDoodhKiShakti carried by existing buyers rather than paid amplification
rows.would_tell_us_it_failed: Within the first 4–6 weeks: shares and saves stay flat and no organic UGC appears, OR sentiment tips negative on the purity/authenticity claim. Existing buyers are watching but not carrying it — advocacy isn't happening, and the format needs a real reason to share, not more paid push.

rows.leading: On-ground: trial-to-switch rate and cost per acquired daily household at RWA stalls. POSM: front-chiller pack pickup and sell-through at stocked stores vs control. Trade: front-of-chiller facings won and distribution depth
rows.lagging: Repeat order rate on acquired households, sustained sell-through uplift at stocked vs control stores, and retained facings after the activation window closes
rows.would_tell_us_it_failed: On-ground: cost per acquired household exceeds the value of a retained daily buyer, or tasters don't convert to a repeat pack. POSM: no sell-through lift at stocked stores vs control within the first cycle. Trade: facings are won during the pitch but lost back to loose milk or Amul within one or two order cycles. Any of these means the activation is buying a spike that doesn't stick — and with the functional 'quality-checked' claim unproven, the chiller assertion may be the weak point. Decide by the end of the first full re-order cycle.
